llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions are generally consistent with an ecommerce review scraper and analyzer, but there are small mismatches (declared pip dependencies with no install spec, and it requires browser access to logged-in sessions) that you should understand before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (review extraction, sentiment, report generation) matches the instructions: browser automation to scrape comments, LLM analysis, and Word/PDF output. Declaring python3 and Chinese NLP/docx/pdf libs is plausible for report generation and Chinese text processing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly requires browser automation, detection of login state, and assisting QR-code login to target e‑commerce sites — this requires access to the user's active browser/session and scraped review content. That is coherent with the skill's purpose, but it does mean the agent will interact with logged‑in sessions and scrape user-visible data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no install spec, no code files). The SKILL.md header lists dependencies as a pip command string, but there is no install spec to ensure those packages are installed. That's an internal inconsistency (expected install instructions are missing) but not evidence of malicious behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables or external credentials. It does rely on the platform-level 'browser' capability and the user's logged-in sessions on Taobao/JD/Pinduoduo, which is proportional to scraping reviews but is sensitive because it exposes session state and site-visible user data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent privileges or modification of other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not combined with other concerning flags.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it claims, but review these points before installing:
- It requires the agent to use browser automation and interact with logged-in ecommerce sessions; only enable it if you accept the agent accessing pages where you are logged in. Consider using a non‑sensitive/testing account first.
- The SKILL.md lists pip packages (jieba, python-docx, fpdf2) but there is no install mechanism; confirm who/what will install those dependencies in your environment (the platform or you). Lack of an install step is a harmless inconsistency but may lead to runtime errors.
- Scraping logged-in sites can expose order/identity data visible on pages — check what data the skill will collect, how long reports are stored, and whether any scraped data is transmitted outside your environment.
- There is no homepage or source repo; if you need stronger assurance, request the author/publisher provide a repository or contact and an explicit install script.
- If you proceed, test with a limited dataset or test account and verify generated reports only contain expected fields.
